artifacts.summary: Pinpoints the exact insertion point (the shared bucketing loop at orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh:1786-1839, common to --dry-run and live) and renaming/reuse strategy (rename WORKTREE_ISOLATED_TASK_TYPES to BUILD_HEAVY_TASK_TYPES, reuse task_selected_for_worktree_isolation() as sole reader) for the Mode 2 build-heavy co-scheduling admission rule, plus test-fixture guidance (Group 32, avoiding the pre-existing file_scope_collision confound documented in Group 31).

memory_candidates.content: In agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, the per-task bucketing loop that builds dispatch_candidates/out_deferred_rows/out_blocked_rows (around line 1786) runs identically for both --dry-run and the live path -- the dry-run/live fork happens later, at the lock-probe/H1/row-builder stage. Any new cross-candidate admission rule (comparing one eligible task against others in the same cycle) placed in that shared loop gets byte-for-byte --dry-run/live parity for free, with no second row builder to keep in sync.

test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh Group 31 discovered that orchestrate-batch-admit.sh's pre-existing in-batch file_scope_collision check (exact-string or directory-prefix match) already defers one of two same-cycle candidates whose file_scope entries overlap -- with no override for in-batch pairs. Any new same-cycle fixture meant to exercise a DIFFERENT admission mechanism must use empty or clearly disjoint file_scope values, or this unrelated pre-existing check silently absorbs the test.
